Follow-ups scheduled to validate networking/VPC requirements and finalize pilot scope.

hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-08 14:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Ravi Patel, Emily Chen - Redwood; Daniel Nguyen, Priya Rao, Tom Baker, Sara Jimenez - Clearcurrent Retail

Auto-summary (may be imperfect): Quick quarterly operational synth. Customer wants stability and predictable economics as they move from pilot to larger rollout; security and VPC are blockers. Redwood to run benchmarks and share security / pricing artifacts.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about an hour, so we'll go through current usage, costs, reliability, then drill into pilot next steps. quick intro round?
[00:12] Daniel Nguyen: Hi all, Daniel here. Head of ML at Clearcurrent. we're running inference for product search assistant and checkout suggestions, mostly on EKS with mixed spot and on-demand gpus, trying to reduce cost while keeping latency under 150ms p50.
[00:28] Priya Rao: Priya, platform. I manage the infra and networking; we'll need to talk about VPC peering and private endpoints.
[00:35] Tom Baker: Tom, ops — focused on SLA and run-rate budgeting.
[00:38] Sara Jimenez: Sara, security PM, will review compliance needs and data flows.
[00:42] Lena Park: Great, from Redwood: Ravi will take the benchmark and SE questions, Emily will coordinate security docs, I'll handle pricing and commercial.

[01:05] Ravi Patel: Quick Q from my side, Daniel — when you say 150ms p50, is that for end-to-end request including your load balancer, or just model token generation?
[01:12] Daniel Nguyen: That's end-to-end from API gateway to response, so includes network hops. Our internal SLO is 200ms p95 and 120ms p50 ideally.

[02:04] Ravi Patel: Got it. A couple clarifications on your workload: average prompt length and token mix? That matters for batching heuristics and KV cache efficiency.
[02:10] Daniel Nguyen: Average prompt about 120 tokens, output 30 tokens typical. Workload is bursty at certain times — promo windows ramp to ~40 rps.

[03:00] Priya Rao: We currently have a multi-az EKS cluster using G4/G5 equivalent instances. We're evaluating if Redwood Dedicated makes sense vs just running our homegrown stack. main thing for us is predictable pricing and network isolation.

[03:26] Lena Park: Totally. Hosted is fastest to start, but Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and better tail latency since you avoid noisy neighbors — though it requires commit. We often recommend a staged approach: start with hosted for feature dev, then move pilot traffic to Dedicated for the burst window testing.

[04:10] Tom Baker: Cost is the blocker. We can't commit to large reserved spend without seeing unit economics. can you show us committed vs usage pricing?
[04:20] Lena Park: We'll put together 3 commit bands and run a cost model for your 3/6/12 month scenarios. We'll also show how batching/quantization recommendations affect unit costs.

[05:02] Sara Jimenez: From security: we need SOC2 attestation, encryption notes, KMS/HSM integration, and audit log retention specifics. Also interested in private control plane options.
[05:15] Emily Chen: We'll send the security packet after the call — includes SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit details, and a network diagram. For private control plane we have an on-prem option and VPC peering; we'll detail the tradeoffs.

[06:00] Ravi Patel: On the technical side: we want to replicate your production-ish tail latencies. We'll run the Redwood Dedicated candidate configuration against your sample traffic. Daniel, can you share a representative pod manifest or concurrency profile?
[06:12] Daniel Nguyen: Yes, I'll share the payloads and a small trace set. we'll scrub PII first.

[07:00] Lena Park: Success criteria — do we have rough acceptance metrics?
[07:05] Tom Baker: If we can see p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms during typical load and cost per 1k tokens under $0.45, we can consider a 3 month commit pilot.

[07:36] Ravi Patel: ok that helps. We'll include p50/p95 and tokens/sec in the benchmark report. We'll also test a quantized 4-bit variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs — note sometimes quantization improves throughput but can bump latency due to kernel patterns, so we'll surface that.

[08:20] Priya Rao: Network – for VPC/private, do you support private endpoints only or full control plane in our VPC? We'll probably need egress controls and allowlist.
[08:30] Emily Chen: We support both: VPC peering and a private control plane option for enterprise. We'll outline which ports and CIDR ranges are needed.

[09:00] Daniel Nguyen: Any concerns about KV cache eviction behavior across long conversations? our product sometimes chains prompts and we rely on prefix caching.
[09:12] Ravi Patel: Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching; eviction policies depend on sequence length distribution. For the benchmark we'll include a chat-style workload to show how caching helps cost and latency. sometimes transcription says 'K V cache' separately — ignore that, it's the same concept.

[10:10] Tom Baker: What about failover? If Dedicated is saturated in a region, can requests fall back to hosted? We need graceful degradation.
[10:18] Lena Park: Yes, smart routing and fallback are options. You can set policy to overflow to hosted variants or to smaller models; we'll show routing policy examples in the runbook.

[11:00] Sara Jimenez: Audit logs — how granular and how long? We need at least 90 days exportable for compliance.
[11:08] Emily Chen: We can provide token-level logs, request/response metadata (redacted), and integrations with your logging sinks. We'll include retention options and export formats in the security packet.

[12:05] Priya Rao: One more on deployment: if we do private control plane, how are upgrades handled? we need maintenance windows and a rollback plan.
[12:14] Ravi Patel: We'll propose a rollout plan with canaries and automatic fallback. For private customers we do coordinated upgrades; we'll provide an upgrade schedule template.

[15:00] [--- 15 minute block condensed: pricing talk + examples of batching/quantization impact, some cross talk, minor transcription noise ---]

[30:02] Lena Park: Recap so far: Redwood to run a 24h benchmark on Dedicated candidate; Emily to share security docs; Lena will send committed pricing bands; customer to provide sample payloads and concurrency profile. Any objections?
[30:15] Daniel Nguyen: no objections. one ask: can you include estimated CPU+GPU utilization graphs so our infra team can map to capacity?
[30:24] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll include utilization and a suggested rightsize. we'll also add a column for expected cost delta if you enable prefix caching aggressively.

[35:00] Tom Baker: On billing granularity — do you bill at token level only, or also for reserved slot hours? how does bursting beyond commit get billed?
[35:12] Lena Park: For Dedicated, commit covers reserved capacity and we have a burst bucket for short-term spikes; overage pricing applies after burst. We'll detail the math in the pricing doc.

[40:00] Sara Jimenez: curious about SSO and RBAC — can we restrict model access per team?
[40:08] Emily Chen: Yes, we support SAML SSO, RBAC per route/model, and token scoping. We'll include example policies.

[45:00] Priya Rao: operationally, how fast can you spin up extra capacity if we have a flash sale?
[45:08] Ravi Patel: Dedicated can autoscale with policy; burst capacity can be used for short windows, but there's a lead time to increase long-term reserved capacity. We'll simulate the flash sale in the benchmark to show how latency behaves.

[50:00] Daniel Nguyen: one practical follow-up — we'll need help mapping our current cost center tags to Redwood billing. can Redwood accept our cost tags or at least provide a mapping?
[50:10] Lena Park: yes, we'll map charges to your tags and include a sample CSV export.

[55:00] Lena Park: Let's lock dates. Ravi, can you run the 24h benchmark and share results by 2027-06-15?
[55:10] Ravi Patel: Yes. I'll need the payload set and concurrency profile by EOD 2027-06-09.
[55:20] Daniel Nguyen: we'll deliver that by the due date.

[58:00] Emily Chen: I'll upload the security packet to the shared drive and cc Sara.
[58:08] Sara Jimenez: ack.

[60:00] Lena Park: Final recap — action items on the calendar, pricing scenarios in a one-pager, security docs, and a benchmark. We'll aim to have a pilot scope doc ready once benchmarks validate latencies. Thanks everyone.
[60:18] Tom Baker: thanks all.
[60:20] Priya Rao: thanks.

[62:00] Meeting ends.
